title: Client-Side Discovery
description: Learn how client-side discovery works and when to use it.

data.text: Client-side discovery is a pattern where the client queries the service registry and selects an instance to call. Netflix Eureka and Consul support this pattern, giving clients full control over load balancing and retry logic.

In client-side discovery, the client is responsible for querying the service registry, selecting an instance, and making the request. The client typically caches the registry data locally and refreshes it periodically. This pattern gives clients flexibility but adds complexity to every client.

data.title: Client-Side Discovery Flow
items: Client queries service registry for available instances
Client caches the registry response locally
Client selects an instance using a load-balancing algorithm
Client makes the request directly to the selected instance

data.title: Common Algorithms
items: Least connections: Route to the instance with fewest active connections
Response time based: Route to the fastest instance
Weighted: Route based on instance capacity

data.title: Netflix Ribbon
data.text: Netflix Ribbon is a popular client-side load balancer that integrates with Eureka. It supports multiple load-balancing algorithms and automatic retries.

items.question: What is the difference between client-side and server-side discovery?
items.answer: Client-side puts load-balancing logic in the client. Server-side uses a load balancer or proxy between clients and services.

items.question: Is client-side discovery more complex?
items.answer: It adds complexity to every client but gives more control. Server-side discovery centralizes the logic but adds a network hop.

items.question: Can I use both patterns?
items.answer: Yes. Kubernetes often uses server-side discovery (kube-proxy), while client-side discovery is common in non-containerized environments.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Client-side discovery gives clients full control over load balancing
Clients cache registry data for resilience
Netflix Eureka and Ribbon are popular implementations
Choose client-side when you need flexible load-balancing logic
data.takeaway: Client-side discovery is powerful but requires every client to implement discovery logic.
